steps.title: Red meat
steps.body: Cabernet's firm tannin and dark fruit call for red meat: steak, roast beef, lamb. Fat and protein soften the tannin. Peppercorn sauce and mushrooms go well. Hard aged cheeses like Comté or aged Cheddar work too. Avoid delicate fish and very spicy food, which make it taste harsh.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Decant young, structured Cabernets for an hour or two. Top Bordeaux and Napa can age 20 to 40 years, gaining cedar, tobacco, leather and earth while tannins soften. Everyday Cabernets are best within three to five years.

steps.prompt: Why does Cabernet Sauvignon go so well with steak?
options: Fat and protein soften its tannin
steps.explanation: Tannin binds to protein and fat, so each softens the other.

steps.body: Old Bordeaux and Napa throw sediment. Stand the bottle upright for a day before opening, then decant slowly in front of a light.

steps.prompt: Which aromas develop in Cabernet as it ages?
steps.explanation: Green apple is a young white wine aroma.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet suits steak, lamb and aged cheese
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees and decant young wines
